title: Residency SLA negotiation — quick cheat sheet
content:
Purpose
Quick reference for sales/solutions/legal/ops when customers ask for residency exceptions that affect SLAs. Designed to be usable in a call or in pre-sales scoping notes. Not canonical legal language — supply to Legal for final wording.

Background/why this matters
- Customers sometimes require service to be physically anchored to a jurisdiction (region pin) but want enterprise SLA parity with cross-region hosted service.
- Full hard-pinning increases operator burden and cost; some compromise options can preserve customer assurance while keeping reasonable ops SLOs.
- This sheet summarizes negotiation levers, technical fallbacks, required telemetry/evidence, and short template language.

High-level negotiation levers (what we can offer quickly)
1) Region-anchored primary + soft-fallback: Primary traffic serves from customer region; automated fallback to warm replica outside-region only on defined emergency and with strict notification windows.
   - Benefits: keeps most traffic local, reduces replication/idle cost.
   - Customer ask to expect: define "emergency" conditions (e.g., >5m outage in-region, sustained 3x latency, infrastructure-level outage).
2) SLA tiers by incident type: separate guarantees for in-region availability vs global control-plane ops (e.g., 99.9% regional compute uptime; 99.95% control-plane reachability).
3) Data-at-rest anchor with mirrored audit evidence: store primary tenant data in-region, periodic signed proofs of residency (hash bundles) sent monthly.
4) Increased MTTR windows for pinned tenants: offer longer mean-time-to-repair targets in exchange for exclusive capacity reservations.
5) Dedicated capacity (Reserved GPU pools) + longer notice for maintenance windows: more predictable throughput, higher unit price.
6) Escrow + third-party audit: for very sensitive customers, arrange escrowed evidence or annual third-party attestation.

Negotiation playbook (concise steps)
- Step 0: classify request (legal-driven vs. ops-preference) and tag the lead with "residency-exception" in the opportunity record.
- Step 1: pre-call prep: run tenant tenancy-cost-estimate (ops tool) and pre-fill expected price delta for reserve capacity + SLA uplift.
- Step 2: on call: confirm exact residency goal (storage-only vs compute-in-region vs control-plane isolation). Ask for: regulatory citation or compliance driver.
- Step 3: propose 2 options (economy vs gold). Always include fallback clause and notification SLA.
- Step 4: capture customer acceptance criteria (how they will test residency) and map to telemetry requirements (see below).
- Step 5: loop in Legal + SRE + Solutions for final clause drafting.

Technical fallbacks we can propose (ops-friendly)
- Soft-fallback with read-only failover: allow read operations from cached read-replicas outside region but writes remain queued to home region for N minutes.
- Graceful degradation policy: limit model concurrency rather than full redirect to alternate region.
- Tiered routing with sticky sessions: preserve session affinity for pinned customers to minimize cross-region leakage.
- Synthetic evidence collector: daily signed manifest of storage snapshots and region metadata.

Telemetry & evidence customers commonly request
- Logs showing "serving node region" for a sample window (example: 2024-10-XX 00:00-03:00).
- Signed hash digest of daily storage snapshot + storage location metadata.
- Network egress/ingress summaries by region per tenant.
- Audit trail for administrative access and config changes.
- Alerting hooks that notify customer security contact on region-fallback events.

Sample SLA snippets (ops + legal friendly, placeholder values)
1) Regional Compute Availability
- "Redwood will ensure 99.5% availability for in-region compute serving the customer's tenant per calendar month. Availability excludes scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice and force majeure events as defined in Section X."
2) Emergency Fallback (example clause)
- "In the event of sustained in-region infrastructure failure exceeding 10 minutes, Redwood may fail over compute to an alternative region. Redwood will provide immediate notification and a post-incident residency report within 72 hours. Customer may require rollback to in-region within the maintenance window subject to capacity availability."
3) Proof-of-Residency Reporting
- "Redwood will produce a signed residency report weekly that includes: list of unique storage blobs anchored in the customer's primary region, list of serving VM IDs and region metadata for sampling windows requested by customer (up to 3 sampling windows per month)."

Operator implications (what SRE/ops should expect)
- Additional on-call paging: region-fallbacks will trigger higher-severity alerts and customer-notify playbooks.
- Capacity planning: reserved pools reduce bin-packing efficiency — include 1.15x buffer for pinned tenants in capacity models.
- Telemetry retention: ensure signed-hash reports retain provenance for 12 months by default.
- Testing: include pinned-tenant scenarios in chaos tests and tabletop exercises (see linked playbook PD-4387).

Pricing levers to present to customer (quick)
- Additive reserved-capacity monthly fee (example: +30–70% depending on utilization and exclusivity).
- SLA uplift fee for higher availability (example: +0.05–0.2% of ARR for 99.9% vs baseline).
- Evidence/Attestation add-on: fixed annual fee for third-party audits or escrow handling.
- Maintenance window premium: customer can buy stricter maintenance scheduling (e.g., no maintenance without 14-day notice).

Common objections & rebuttals (short)
- "We need zero fallback." -> "Zero fallback is operationally risky and expensive. We can offer near-zero with dedicated on-prem or air-gapped installer + legal attestation; will need >QBR planning and premium pricing."
- "How do we prove you didn’t touch data outside the region?" -> "We provide signed daily manifests, access logs, and optional third-party attestations. For very sensitive customers we recommend an on-prem package."

Open questions / items to escalate to Legal or Product
- Standardizing "emergency" definition: SRE proposal vs Legal definition. (Action: Priya to draft proposal by 2024-12-01).
- Acceptable sample size for residency reports (how many VM IDs / blobs equals 'proof').
- Template for customer notification cadence (immediate + 24h + post-mortem timeline).

Quick templates to drop in proposals (fill placeholders)
- Option A (soft anchor): Primary region: {REGION}. Availability (in-region compute): 99.5%/mo. Fallback: permitted after 10 minutes of sustained outage, with notification to {SECURITY_CONTACT}. Weekly signed residency report included. Pricing delta: {PRICE_DELTA}.
- Option B (reserved capacity): Dedicated pool in {REGION}, Availability: 99.9%/mo, maintenance-with-notice: 14 days, monthly usage commitment: {COMMITMENT}, third-party audit: opt-in. Pricing delta: {PRICE_DELTA_HIGH}.

Useful links / references
- Confluence: region-sla-templates (linked above)
- Jira: PD-4387 (residency audit automation backlog)
- Slack channel: #residency-ops (use for escalations during negotiation)

Notes to self
- Keep this doc lean — sales wants quick bullets on calls. Convert to a one-pager for Solutions team.
- Add a short checklist doc for SRE runbook triggers when fallback occurs (follow-on doc: create PD ticket).
summary: Cheat sheet for negotiating residency-related SLA exceptions with customers. Includes negotiation levers, operator impact, sample SLA clauses, telemetry requirements, and quick proposal templates.
